rulesNote: Facts below were checked against the funder pages on November 26, 2026. The daily morning check reads official pages and Grants.gov and changes a status line only when the page itself changes.

grants.name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants
grants.deadlineLabel: Cycle 3 deadline is November 30, 2026. Next fiscal year cycles open February 1, May 1, and August 1.
grants.amountLabel: $250 to $5,000 per facility per fiscal year.
grants.summary: Local Walmart stores and distribution centers award cash grants of $250 to $5,000 to county and city agencies in their service area. Shelbyville has both Walmart Supercenter #656 and Walmart Distribution Center #6062.
grants.why: Walmart Spark Good guidelines list counties and municipal agencies as eligible government entities. Applicants must serve the same area as the facility. Shelbyville has Supercenter #656 at 1880 N. Main St. and Distribution Center #6062 at 285 Frank Martin Rd., on the same road as the EMS station.
rules: Set up a Spark Good account on Walmart.com and complete verification through Deed before you apply. Use the same work email for both.
Ask for $250 to $5,000. You may receive one grant per Walmart facility in the same fiscal year (February 1 through January 31).
Shelbyville has two separate facilities. You can file one request with Supercenter #656 and one request with Distribution Center #6062.
Facility managers recommend local grants. A short call or visit to the local manager helps before you submit.
If approved, you must provide county banking details within 21 days for electronic payment through JP Morgan.
sources: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants guidelines, checked November 26, 2026. Cycle 3 last day to submit is November 30.
Walmart Spark Good Government Entity one-pager, non-501(c)(3) county and municipal eligibility
Walmart Supercenter #656 (1880 N. Main St.) and Walmart Distribution Center #6062 (285 Frank Martin Rd.), Shelbyville, TN

grants.name: Gary Sinise Foundation, First Responders Outreach
grants.deadlineLabel: Open year-round with rolling review. Applications stay under review for up to 6 months.
grants.amountLabel: Set by the equipment or training request. No dollar cap is posted on the guidelines.
grants.summary: This private foundation accepts rolling requests from EMS agencies for equipment and training. It prioritizes volunteer and underfunded departments, so a paid county service faces stiff competition.
grants.why: The foundation's First Responders Outreach guidelines explicitly name Emergency Medical Service organizations as eligible first responder departments.
rules: Requests are limited to equipment and training. Building, construction, utility, land, and operating costs are not eligible.
Limit is one application per calendar year, whether the prior request was approved or denied.
Applications stay open for approval for 6 months. The foundation contacts you only if approved, if it has questions, or after the 6-month period ends.
Priority goes to volunteer, low, and underfunded departments. Keep the request focused on an essential equipment or training gap.
Send questions to firstresponder@garysinisefoundation.org.
sources: Gary Sinise Foundation First Responders Outreach Grant Guidelines, checked November 26, 2026

grants.name: Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation
grants.deadlineLabel: Portal opens January 14, 2027 at 2:00 p.m. ET. It stops after 600 applications.
grants.amountLabel: $15,000 to $25,000 is the usual range. Requests over $40,000 are rejected. They do not fund part of a quote.
grants.summary: This private foundation buys lifesaving equipment for EMS. The next opening is January 14, 2027. Have the quote ready and submit the same afternoon. The portal often fills the same day.
grants.why: The foundation accepts EMS, fire, and law enforcement. A county ambulance service can apply. There is a Firehouse Subs in the region, and the award stays with the department.
rules: One request per organization. If you have received an award, wait 4 years from the funding date before you apply again. That waiting period starts with the January 2027 quarter.
They do not reimburse equipment you already bought.
They do not fund power-load stretchers, naloxone, drones, body cameras, or exercise equipment.
You need one official vendor quote with the foundation's required quote details, plus a current budget, balance sheet, or audit that shows the county or department name.
The portal opens at 2:00 p.m. ET on January 14, 2027, April 15, 2027, and July 15, 2027. Dates can change. The morning check reads the foundation page.
sources: Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation application page, checked November 26, 2026. The portal was closed and listed a reopen time of January 14, 2027 at 2:00 p.m. ET.

grants.name: Tennessee Highway Safety Office, EMS
grants.deadlineLabel: Applications open March 1 and close March 31. The 2026 window has passed. Plan on March 1, 2027, and confirm the date on the THSO page.
grants.amountLabel: Peer EMS awards in the FFY 2026 list were about $12,500 for extrication equipment and under $17,000 for training.
grants.matchLabel: Check the current THSO notice. Do not assume a match.
grants.summary: THSO funds EMS training and extrication equipment in rural counties that rank in the top 65 for crashes. The goal is care in the first hour after a crash.
grants.why: Bedford County ranked 23rd of 95 counties for overall crash rate in the 2021 through 2025 rankings published by the Tennessee Department of Safety in February 2026. The state also treated the county as eligible for the rural ambulance allocation.
rules: The agency must be in a rural county and in the top 65 for overall crashes. Bedford meets the crash rank. Confirm the rural box when the portal opens.
You must attach three years of crash numbers for Bedford County from the THSO dashboard, plus a comparison that shows the problem is above average.
Fund training or extrication tools. Do not ask THSO for a new ambulance.
Apply at THSOGrants.org during the March window.
Recent awards to other county EMS and rescue agencies clustered around $12,500. A request in that range matches what THSO has funded.
sources: Tennessee Traffic Safety Resource Service, Grant Application Process, EMS program area
Tennessee Department of Safety county rankings, 2021 through 2025, revised February 12, 2026. Bedford overall crash rate rank 23.
FFY 2026 THSO grant awards list

grants.name: Assistance to Firefighters Grant, ambulance
grants.deadlineLabel: FY 2025 window closed June 22, 2026. The next window is not posted yet.
grants.amountLabel: Ambulance. FEMA sets aside part of the vehicle money for ambulances.
grants.matchLabel: 10 percent cash match. In-kind match is not allowed.
grants.summary: This is the main federal grant for a county ambulance service that is not part of a fire department or a hospital. It can buy a new ambulance to replace an old front-line unit.
grants.why: Bedford County EMS is a county ambulance service. It provides medical transport. It is not a hospital. Shelbyville fire does not run the county ambulance service. That is the FEMA test for a nonaffiliated EMS organization.
rules: You may submit one Vehicle Acquisition application, one Operations and Safety application, and one regional application. Do not request the same vehicle twice.
Ambulances are a high priority vehicle for nonaffiliated EMS. The unit must meet NFPA 1900 or GSA KKK-A-1822F.
The service area population is 55,273. For a population from 20,001 through 1,000,000, FEMA divides the total cost by 1.10 to get the federal share. The county pays the rest in cash.
Replace the oldest front-line ambulance. Do not use this grant to duplicate the Rural Health Transformation ambulance awarded in 2026.
Give the year, mileage, and VIN of the unit you will replace. Unsafe units that you certify as removed cannot go back into emergency service.
Drivers must be trained to the DOT emergency vehicle operator course, or an equal course, before the new ambulance arrives.
Apply in FEMA GO. The authorized official has to certify the application.
sources: FEMA FY 2025 AFG Notice of Funding Opportunity, funding opportunity DHS-25-GPD-044-00-98
FEMA Assistance to Firefighters Grants page, checked November 26, 2026. The FY 2025 application period is closed.
U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts, Bedford County, Tennessee, July 1, 2025 population estimate 55,273

grants.name: Assistance to Firefighters Grant, equipment and training
grants.deadlineLabel: FY 2025 window closed June 22, 2026. The next window is not posted yet.
grants.amountLabel: Monitors, radios, PPE, or training. A micro grant is a federal request of $75,000 or less.
grants.matchLabel: 10 percent cash match. In-kind match is not allowed.
grants.summary: The same FEMA program can fund cardiac monitors, portable radios, EMS protective gear, or EMT and paramedic training. File this only if you are not asking for the same items on a vehicle application.
grants.why: A county transport service that is not hospital-based and not fire-based can apply for Operations and Safety. Training priorities for this type of service include EMT, AEMT, and paramedic courses.
rules: One Operations and Safety application per cycle. A micro grant of $75,000 or less in federal funds does not stop you from also requesting a vehicle.
Monitors should match the number of ALS transport units. Portable radios must meet P25 rules and the Tennessee interoperability plan.
EMS turnout gear has to meet the current NFPA edition. Structural firefighting gear is not eligible for a nonaffiliated EMS service.
Power-load systems are a poor fit here if you can fund a monitor or training instead. Ask for the item your oldest inventory actually needs.
The 10 percent cash match uses the same FEMA formula as the vehicle grant.
Apply in FEMA GO. The authorized official has to certify the application.
sources: FEMA FY 2025 AFG Notice of Funding Opportunity
FEMA Assistance to Firefighters Grants page, checked November 26, 2026

grants.name: SAMHSA Rural Emergency Medical Services Training (R-EMS)
grants.deadlineLabel: FY 2026 window (TI-26-004) closed July 16, 2026. The FY 2027 notice is not posted yet.
grants.amountLabel: Up to $300,000 per year for up to 2 years (FY 2026 NOFO TI-26-004).
grants.summary: This federal grant funds rural EMS recruitment, EMT and paramedic licensing courses, EMS equipment, OSHA PPE, mental health and substance use training, and overdose reversal medications.
grants.why: Under 42 U.S.C. § 290ee-10 and FY 2026 NOFO TI-26-004, local government EMS agencies (both fire-based and non-fire-based) serving a nonmetropolitan statistical area are eligible. Bedford County is the Shelbyville, TN Micropolitan Statistical Area, classified as nonmetropolitan by OMB, BLS, and TNECD.
rules: Annual budgets cannot exceed $300,000 in direct and indirect costs per year, for up to 2 years. No local match is required.
Required uses include training EMS staff for state or federal certification, acquiring EMS equipment, and training staff on mental health and substance use emergencies.
Allowed uses also include recruitment and retention, OSHA-required PPE, technology-based training, and FDA-approved overdose reversal drugs or devices.
Send a Public Health System Impact Statement (PHSIS) to state and local health agencies by the application deadline.
Requires an active SAM.gov registration and UEI. Apply on Grants.gov when the next notice posts.
sources: SAMHSA FY 2026 R-EMS Notice of Funding Opportunity TI-26-004 (CFDA 93.490), closed July 16, 2026
42 U.S.C. § 290ee-10, Rural emergency medical service training and equipment assistance program
OMB, BLS (May 2025 OEWS), and TNECD classification of Bedford County as nonmetropolitan (Shelbyville, TN Micropolitan Statistical Area)

grants.name: Tennessee CDBG, public health and safety
grants.funder: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development
grants.deadlineLabel: The 2026 applications were due April 10, 2026. The 2027 round was briefed on October 22, 2026. A 2027 due date is not posted yet.
grants.amountLabel: Up to $420,000 for an equipment project such as an ambulance. Up to $1,000,000 if construction is most of the project.
grants.matchLabel: County match is the ability-to-pay rate, from 5 percent to 25 percent. Get Bedford County's rate from TNECD. Do not guess it.
grants.summary: The state CDBG program names ambulances, emergency communications, and other public health and safety projects as eligible. Bedford County can apply because it is not a HUD entitlement county.
grants.why: Eligible applicants are Tennessee cities and counties that do not get CDBG directly from HUD. Bedford County is not on the entitlement list. A county may apply for a project inside the county. Only one regular-round application is allowed, and a government with an open regular-round grant cannot apply.
rules: At least 51 percent of the people who benefit must have low or moderate income, using the HUD figure or a TNECD income survey. If the countywide figure is under 51 percent, do not file a countywide ambulance project until TNECD accepts another method.
The county commission has to pass a resolution before you submit. An application without the resolution is ineligible.
Hold a public meeting first. Advertise it in the newspaper at least 14 full days ahead, with a nondiscrimination statement and a disability contact.
An ambulance with no installation work can use the exempt environmental certification.
Administration is capped at 6.5 percent of the grant. TNECD does not hold money for cost overruns.
File in the TNECD SmartSimple portal when the 2027 round opens.
sources: Tennessee State CDBG Program 2026 Application Notices
TNECD CDBG page, 2027 public meeting held October 22, 2026

grants.name: Tennessee Opioid Abatement Council, EMS and county funds
grants.deadlineLabel: Community Grants Cycle 3 closed April 6, 2026 (awards expected January 15, 2027). Cycle 4 is planned for October 2027. Counties also receive annual Quarter 1 opioid abatement payments.
grants.amountLabel: Community Grants cap at $1,000,000 per year for a single applicant (12, 24, or 36 months) and cannot exceed the agency's annual operating budget.
grants.matchLabel: No match required. Reimbursement-based. Indirect costs capped at 15 percent.
grants.summary: Tennessee's Opioid Abatement Council funds EMS post-overdose care connections, peer support partnerships, responder training, and overdose data work. You can also ask the Bedford County Commission about the county's annual Quarter 1 opioid abatement share.
grants.why: Cycle 3 rules explicitly allow established Tennessee governmental agencies to apply. Remediation Strategy CC9 names Emergency Medical Systems connecting overdose patients to treatment. Separately, T.C.A. § 33-11-103 sends 35 percent of trust fund proceeds directly to Tennessee's 95 counties each year.
rules: Eligible EMS strategies include Strategy CC9 (post-overdose care and peer support connections), BB11 and KK1 (responder training), and FF6 (overdose and naloxone data systems).
Agencies must have operated at least 24 months. A Community Grant winner cannot apply in two consecutive cycles.
Community Grants are reimbursement-based, payor of last resort, and cannot pay for past projects.
File Community Grants in the State of Tennessee Sub-Recipient Grant Management Enterprise Solution portal when Cycle 4 opens.
For immediate local needs such as naloxone or overdose response training, coordinate with the Bedford County Commission on the county's annual Quarter 1 opioid abatement disbursement.
sources: Tennessee OAC Community Grants Cycle 3 Announcement of Funding, revised February 13, 2026 (Cycle 4 planned for October 2027)
Tennessee OAC Current Community Grants page, checked November 26, 2026
Tennessee OAC County Funding page, T.C.A. § 33-11-103 annual Quarter 1 county disbursements

grants.name: Rural Health Transformation, Round 2 ambulance and next EMS project
grants.deadlineLabel: Round 1 ambulance ($305,461) is awarded. Round 2 rural ambulance grants are in legislative review as of November 18, 2026. No new application packet is posted yet.
grants.amountLabel: Round 1 provided up to $305,461 for one ambulance and one power-lift system. Round 2 and later competitive amounts depend on the official packet.
grants.matchLabel: Reimbursement-based. Each notice sets its own match rules. Do not assume there is no match on competitive rounds.
grants.summary: Track two items here. First, watch for the Round 2 rural county ambulance grant packet after legislative review finishes. Second, prepare a competitive Last Mile Teams or workforce concept without duplicating the Round 1 unit.
grants.why: Bedford County EMS received the Round 1 rural county ambulance allocation ($305,461). On November 18, 2026, TASA reported that TDOH is completing legislative-committee review for Round 2 ambulance grants, with packets estimated in 30 to 45 days. TDH's rural health page also lists Last Mile Teams covering ambulances, community paramedicine, and mobile health.
rules: Do not duplicate the Round 1 ambulance already funded in 2026.
Watch TDH and TASA notices for the official Round 2 rural county ambulance packet and eligibility rules.
Competitive RHTP rounds are reimbursement-based, cap administrative costs at 10 percent, and require registration with the State of Tennessee.
Send questions to RuralHealth@tn.gov and watch tn.gov/health/rural.
The morning check watches the rural health page for a new notice that names EMS, ambulances, or the workforce.
sources: Tennessee Department of Health rural health page, Last Mile Teams and Budget Period 1-5 schedule
TASA Update: Round #2 RHT County Ambulance Program, November 18, 2026 (legislative committee review underway)
Bedford County Financial Management Committee reports, June 23, 2026 and September 23, 2026

grants.name: Tennessee State Ambulance Equipment Grant
grants.funder: Tennessee Department of Health, Office of EMS
grants.deadlineLabel: Non-recurring legislative appropriation. No 2027 round is posted yet. Watch the 2027 General Assembly session and TDH Office of EMS notices.
grants.amountLabel: In 2025, the General Assembly appropriated $5 million, or about $23,000 per licensed ambulance service.
grants.matchLabel: Set by the state request for application if funded.
grants.summary: Tennessee has periodically funded equipment grants for every licensed ambulance service in the state to buy stretchers, cardiac monitors, or essential gear. TACIR recommended in September 2026 that the legislature make this grant recurring.
grants.why: Bedford County EMS is a state-licensed primary Category A ambulance service. When the General Assembly funds this program, licensed Tennessee ambulance services can apply directly.
rules: Funding was non-recurring in 2023 and 2025 and skipped in 2024. It opens only if the General Assembly appropriates money.
Keep a current vendor quote ready for essential ambulance equipment such as a monitor, stretcher, or pediatric transport device.
Watch TDH Office of EMS emails and the 2027 Tennessee General Assembly budget.
sources: TACIR Final Report, Improving Tennessee's Ambulance Services through Increased Funding, Collaboration, and Training, September 2026 ($5 million appropriated in 2025, about $23,000 per licensed service)

grants.name: Homeland Security Grant through Bedford County EMA
grants.deadlineLabel: TEMA posts the deadline in the EM Grants Portal when a cycle opens. EMS does not apply alone.
grants.amountLabel: Set by the state allocation and the local EMA. Ask for a preparedness project, not a routine ambulance.
grants.summary: Radios, mass-casualty equipment, training, and exercises can be funded. The request has to go through the Bedford County emergency management agency.
grants.why: TEMA tells departments to work through the local emergency management agency. A county EMS service can ask the EMA to carry a project that prepares the county for terrorism and other hazards.
rules: Do not send this request straight to TEMA. Send it to the Bedford County EMA and ask the EMA to submit it.
The project has to support prevention, protection, response, or recovery. A replacement ambulance for daily 911 work does not fit.
Radios bought with this money have to meet interoperability rules.
Equipment has to be inventoried and tagged.
The morning check reads the TEMA page for a posted deadline.
sources: TEMA Homeland Security Grant Program page, checked November 26, 2026

notAFit.name: USDA Community Facilities grant
notAFit.reason: The grant is for rural places of 20,000 people or fewer. The Census Bureau estimates Shelbyville at 26,146 people as of July 1, 2025. The station at 119 Frank Martin Road is inside the city, so this grant is not a fit.

notAFit.name: FEMA SAFER staffing grant
notAFit.reason: SAFER hires firefighters for fire departments. A county ambulance service that is not a fire department cannot file as a fire department.

notAFit.name: FEMA Fire Prevention and Safety (FP&S) grant
notAFit.reason: Under FEMA's FY 2025 Federal Register notice, nonaffiliated EMS organizations are excluded from FP&S, even though they can apply for AFG.

notAFit.name: Appalachian Regional Commission
notAFit.reason: Bedford County is not an Appalachian Regional Commission county. Shelbyville sits outside that service area.

notAFit.name: Motorola Solutions Foundation Annual Grants
notAFit.reason: Counties and municipal EMS departments cannot apply directly. Only a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or NCES school district can be the lead applicant, and equipment cannot be most of the budget.

notAFit.name: Tennessee Rescue Squad Grant Program (TDCI / SFMO)
notAFit.reason: Starting in 2026 under the Rescue Squad Recognition Act, applicants must hold a Secretary of State rescue squad charter and a State Fire Marshal's Office recognition certificate. A county ambulance service without a separate chartered rescue squad cannot file directly.
